proof.text: The subspace $xN$ is graded: if $m=\sum_jm_j$ is the finite homogeneous decomposition of an element of $N$, then $xm=\sum_jxm_j$ and $xm_j\in N_{j+1}$. Comparing homogeneous components gives $(xN)\cap N_0=0$ and $(xN)\cap N_{n+1}=xN_n$. It also shows that the images of the $N_j$ in $C$ have direct sum: if a finite sum $\sum_jv_j$ lies in $xN$, comparing its components gives $v_j\in xN$ individually. These images span $C$, so they give exactly its quotient grading. Multiplication by $x$ is $k$-linear and restricts to an injective map $N_n\to N_{n+1}$. The map $N_{n+1}\to C_{n+1}$ is surjective by the definition of $C_{n+1}$ and has kernel $xN_n$ by the preceding component comparison. This proves the asserted exact sequence in every degree, including $n=0$.

proof.text: Put $U=xN_n\subseteq N_{n+1}$. The maps $N_n\to U$, $m\mapsto xm$, and $N_{n+1}/U\to C_{n+1}$, $v+U\mapsto\overline v$, are linear bijections: the first uses the assumed injectivity; the second uses precisely the kernel and surjectivity proved in step 1. A linear bijection sends a basis to a basis. Since $N_{n+1}$ is finite-dimensional, [lem-trf-vector-space-quotient-dimension] shows that $U$, $N_{n+1}/U$, and hence $C_{n+1}$ are finite-dimensional and gives $\dim_kC_{n+1}+\dim_kN_n=\dim_kN_{n+1}$. Rearranging in $\mathbf Z$, or after embedding the dimensions in $\mathbf Q$, gives the stated difference formula.

proof.text: Now assume $\dim_kC_n=P(n)$ for all $n\ge d$. Regard dimensions as rational numbers and put $H(n)=\dim_kN_n$, $f(t)=H(d+t)$, and $A(X)=P(X+d+1)$. Step 2 gives $f(t+1)-f(t)=P(d+t+1)=A(t)$ for every $t\ge0$, because $d+t+1\ge d$. Choose a natural number $b$ strictly exceeding $\deg A$ (take $b=1+\operatorname{natdeg}A$, also when $A=0$). Apply [lem-trf-rational-sequence-polynomial-forward-difference] to obtain $R\in\mathbf Q[X]$ with $R(t)=f(t)$ for all natural $t$. Set $B(X)=R(X-d)$, $c=0$, and $e=d$. For $n\ge e$ the natural number $t=n-d$ satisfies $d+t=n$, so $B(n)+c=R(t)=H(n)$.

proof.text: For every natural $n\ge d+1$, both $n$ and $n-1$ lie in the range of the formula just proved. Hence $B(n)-B(n-1)=H(n)-H(n-1)=\dim_kC_n=P(n)$ by step 2. The rationals represented by the integers $n\ge d+1$ are pairwise distinct and form an infinite set. Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-infinite-evaluation-identity] over the integral domain $\mathbf Q$ to the polynomials $B(X)-B(X-1)$ and $P(X)$; this proves their equality as polynomials. No nonzero assumption on $P$ or $N$ was used. In particular the construction also covers $P=0$, when $H$ is eventually constant, and $N=0$, when all the displayed dimensions vanish.

title: Polynomial lifting through injective multiplication in degree one
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be a standard graded $k$-algebra [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra], and let $N=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}N_n$ be an $S$-module with a direct-sum decomposition into finite-dimensional $k$-subspaces such that $S_iN_j\subseteq N_{i+j}$. Let $x\in S_1$ and assume that $m\mapsto xm$ is injective on $N$. Give $C=N/xN$ its quotient grading $C_n=\operatorname{im}(N_n\to C)$. For every $n\ge0$ there is an exact sequence of finite-dimensional $k$-spaces $0\to N_n\xrightarrow{x}N_{n+1}\to C_{n+1}\to0$, and consequently $\dim_kN_{n+1}-\dim_kN_n=\dim_kC_{n+1}$. If $P\in\mathbf Q[X]$ and $d\in\mathbf N$ satisfy $\dim_kC_n=P(n)$ for all $n\ge d$, then there are $B\in\mathbf Q[X]$, $c\in\mathbf Q$, and $e\in\mathbf N$ such that $B(X)-B(X-1)=P(X)$ as polynomials and $\dim_kN_n=B(n)+c$ for all $n\ge e$. The polynomial $P$ and the module $N$ may be zero.
